booster.note: The booster landed on A Shortfall of Gravitas (droneship), 600 km downrange.

capsule.reason: Nothing comes back to Earth on this mission.

wave_height_m.missing_reason: Not published by the launch provider; the team can enter the limit it is given.

wind_m_s.missing_reason: Not published by the launch provider; the team can enter the limit it is given.

model_check.atmosphere: NRLMSISE-00, an empirical model of the air’s density at each height and place, given that day’s solar radio flux (10.7 cm: 174.1 solar flux units the day before, 149.3 averaged over 81 days) and geomagnetic activity (ap 4 at the time). The U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 takes its place when a day has none of these.
sources: Francis et al., Entry, Descent, and Landing Analysis for the OSIRIS-REx Sample Return Capsule (AAS 24), https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20240000629
Wibben et al., AAS 24-058, Table 12 (reconstructed entry state)
Mitcheltree et al. 1997 and Wilmoth et al. 1997 (Stardust capsule shape and axial force)
Picone et al., NRLMSISE-00 empirical model of the atmosphere: statistical comparisons and scientific issues, J. Geophys. Res. 107(A12), 1468 (2002), doi:10.1029/2002JA009430 (run through pymsis)
Emmert et al., NRLMSIS 2.1: an empirical model of nitric oxide incorporated into MSIS, J. Geophys. Res. Space Physics 127, e2022JA030896 (2022) (the comparison run)
NASA SPDF, OMNI hourly data: the 10.7 cm solar flux and the 3-hour ap from NOAA NGDC

National Weather Service radiosonde, Salt Lake City (KSLC, WMO 72572), 24 September 2023 12 UTC, from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/json/raob.py?ts=202309241200&station=KSLC
model_check.note: From OSIRIS-REx’s reconstructed entry state, the entry model lands its capsule 12.1 km from where the recovery team found it (9.4 to 14.8 km over the published drag range; the limit is 10 km, not met). It flies through NRLMSISE-00 for that day. With other air the distance is U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976, 9.5 km (6.7 to 12.2); NRLMSIS 2.1, 6.6 km (3.9 to 9.3). The mission’s own simulation from the same state was 8.9 km off with its pre-flight atmosphere and 3.5 km with the day’s reconstructed one. Its 99 % landing area, 51.2 by 21.8 km, holds the real landing point.

parts.note: From the launch azimuth and the published downrange distance, ±12 km.
